questions.prompt: In which modern country are the Great Pyramids of Giza located?
questions.hint: They stand near Cairo.
questions.explanation: The Great Pyramids of Giza were built in ancient Egypt on the west bank of the Nile.

questions.prompt: What value does the Roman numeral X represent?
questions.hint: It is twice V.
questions.explanation: In Roman numerals, X represents the number 10.

questions.prompt: Julius Caesar was assassinated on a date traditionally called what?
questions.hint: It falls on March 15.
questions.explanation: Caesar was killed on March 15, 44 BCE, a date known as the Ides of March.

questions.prompt: The ancient Olympic Games originated in which civilization?
questions.hint: The games were associated with Olympia.
questions.explanation: The ancient Olympic Games were held at Olympia in Greece.

questions.prompt: The Rosetta Stone was crucial in deciphering which writing system?
questions.hint: It carried the same decree in three scripts.
questions.explanation: The Rosetta Stone helped scholars decipher Egyptian hieroglyphs by comparing them with Greek and Demotic text.

questions.prompt: Hammurabi is best known for a law code associated with which ancient kingdom?
questions.hint: His capital stood in Mesopotamia.
questions.explanation: Hammurabi ruled Babylon and is associated with one of the best-known surviving ancient law codes.

questions.prompt: The Punic Wars were fought mainly between Rome and which rival power?
questions.hint: The rival city stood in North Africa.
questions.explanation: Rome fought three Punic Wars against Carthage.

questions.prompt: Who is traditionally regarded as the first emperor to unify China?
questions.hint: His dynasty gave China its English name.
questions.explanation: Qin Shi Huang unified the warring states in 221 BCE and became China's first emperor.

questions.prompt: The Battle of Marathon occurred during wars between the Greeks and which empire?
questions.hint: Darius I ruled the invading power.
questions.explanation: Marathon was a major Greek victory over a Persian invasion in 490 BCE.

questions.prompt: The famous Library of Alexandria was located in which ancient kingdom?
questions.hint: Its city was founded by Alexander the Great.
questions.explanation: The Library of Alexandria flourished in Ptolemaic Egypt.

questions.prompt: Ashoka the Great ruled which empire?
questions.hint: It controlled much of the Indian subcontinent in the 3rd century BCE.
questions.explanation: Ashoka was the third ruler of the Maurya Empire.

questions.prompt: Linear B was used to write an early form of which language?
questions.hint: It appears on Mycenaean palace tablets.
questions.explanation: Linear B records Mycenaean Greek, making it the earliest attested form of Greek.

questions.prompt: The Achaemenid Royal Road famously linked Sardis with which imperial center?
questions.hint: The eastern terminus was in present-day Iran.
questions.explanation: The Royal Road connected Sardis in Anatolia with Susa, an Achaemenid administrative center.

questions.prompt: At the Battle of Actium, Octavian defeated the forces of Mark Antony and whom?
questions.hint: She was the last active ruler of Ptolemaic Egypt.
questions.explanation: Octavian defeated Mark Antony and Cleopatra at Actium in 31 BCE.

questions.prompt: The Antikythera mechanism was primarily designed to model or predict what?
questions.hint: Its gears tracked the heavens.
questions.explanation: The Antikythera mechanism used complex gears to calculate astronomical positions and eclipse cycles.

questions.prompt: The Black Death was primarily caused by which disease?
questions.hint: The bacterium Yersinia pestis is responsible.
questions.explanation: The Black Death was a devastating pandemic of plague.

questions.prompt: The Magna Carta was first sealed in which year?
questions.hint: King John agreed to it in the early 13th century.
questions.explanation: King John sealed Magna Carta at Runnymede in 1215.

questions.prompt: Who is associated with developing movable-type printing in 15th-century Europe?
questions.hint: He printed a famous Bible.
questions.explanation: Johannes Gutenberg developed a practical movable-type printing system in Mainz.

questions.prompt: Joan of Arc fought on behalf of which kingdom?
questions.hint: She helped lift the siege of Orléans.
questions.explanation: Joan of Arc supported the French crown during the Hundred Years' War.

questions.prompt: The Renaissance is conventionally said to have begun in which region?
questions.hint: Florence was one of its great centers.
questions.explanation: The Renaissance first flourished in Italian city-states.

questions.prompt: Constantinople fell to the Ottoman Empire in which year?
questions.hint: The date marks the end of the Byzantine Empire.
questions.explanation: Sultan Mehmed II captured Constantinople in 1453.

questions.prompt: What was the capital of the Aztec Empire?
questions.hint: It stood on an island in Lake Texcoco.
questions.explanation: Tenochtitlan was the Aztec capital on the site of modern Mexico City.

questions.prompt: The Treaty of Tordesillas divided newly claimed lands mainly between Spain and which country?
questions.hint: The other signatory led early voyages around Africa.
questions.explanation: The 1494 treaty divided overseas spheres between Spain and Portugal.

questions.prompt: Which Ottoman sultan is commonly known as 'the Magnificent' in the West?
questions.hint: He ruled during the empire's 16th-century zenith.
questions.explanation: Suleiman I is widely called Suleiman the Magnificent.

questions.prompt: Which settlement ended the Thirty Years' War in 1648?
questions.hint: It consisted of treaties signed at Münster and Osnabrück.
questions.explanation: The Peace of Westphalia ended the Thirty Years' War in 1648.

questions.prompt: The Tokugawa shogunate was established in which year?
questions.hint: Tokugawa Ieyasu became shogun shortly after Sekigahara.
questions.explanation: Tokugawa Ieyasu received the title of shogun in 1603.

questions.prompt: The 1618 Defenestration of Prague helped trigger which conflict?

choices.text: The War of the Spanish Succession

questions.hint: Bohemian nobles threw imperial officials from a castle window.
questions.explanation: The Defenestration of Prague was a key spark of the Thirty Years' War.

questions.prompt: Which dynasty made Twelver Shi'a Islam the state religion of Iran?
questions.hint: Shah Ismail I founded it.
questions.explanation: The Safavids established Twelver Shi'ism as Iran's state religion.

questions.prompt: Which Mughal emperor is especially associated with religious accommodation and administrative reform?
questions.hint: He created the imperial rank system called mansabdari.
questions.explanation: Akbar expanded the Mughal Empire and pursued broad religious and administrative policies.

questions.prompt: The Peace of Augsburg endorsed which principle within the Holy Roman Empire?

choices.text: The ruler's religion could determine the territory's religion

questions.hint: The Latin phrase begins cuius regio.
questions.explanation: The settlement's principle, cuius regio, eius religio, allowed rulers to choose Catholicism or Lutheranism for their territories.

questions.prompt: In what year did the Berlin Wall fall?
questions.hint: It fell shortly before German reunification.
questions.explanation: The Berlin Wall opened on November 9, 1989.

questions.prompt: The French Revolution began in which year?
questions.hint: The Bastille was stormed that summer.
questions.explanation: The French Revolution began in 1789.

questions.prompt: The RMS Titanic sank in which year?
questions.hint: It struck an iceberg on its maiden voyage.
questions.explanation: Titanic sank in April 1912.

questions.prompt: The assassination of which figure helped trigger World War I?
questions.hint: He was killed in Sarajevo.
questions.explanation: The assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand in June 1914 helped set off the July Crisis.

questions.prompt: India became independent from British rule in which year?
questions.hint: Partition occurred at the same time.
questions.explanation: British India was partitioned into India and Pakistan in 1947.

questions.prompt: The Cuban Missile Crisis occurred in which year?
questions.hint: It brought the United States and Soviet Union close to nuclear war.
questions.explanation: The Cuban Missile Crisis unfolded in October 1962.

questions.prompt: The Meiji Restoration transformed which country?
questions.hint: It restored imperial rule in 1868.
questions.explanation: The Meiji Restoration ended Tokugawa rule and launched rapid modernization in Japan.

questions.prompt: The Suez Canal opened to shipping in which year?
questions.hint: It linked the Mediterranean and Red seas.
questions.explanation: The Suez Canal officially opened in 1869.

questions.prompt: The 1955 Bandung Conference brought together countries mainly from which two continents?
questions.hint: It became a landmark of postcolonial cooperation.
questions.explanation: Bandung gathered Asian and African states and helped inspire the Non-Aligned Movement.

questions.prompt: The Dreyfus Affair was a major political scandal in which country?
questions.hint: It centered on a Jewish army officer falsely accused of treason.
questions.explanation: The Dreyfus Affair divided France in the late 19th and early 20th centuries.

questions.prompt: The Treaty of Brest-Litovsk removed which country from World War I?
questions.hint: The Bolshevik government signed it in 1918.
questions.explanation: Soviet Russia signed Brest-Litovsk with the Central Powers and left the war.

questions.prompt: The Marshall Plan was intended mainly to support the recovery of which region?
questions.hint: It followed World War II.
questions.explanation: The Marshall Plan provided U.S. aid for European reconstruction after World War II.

questions.prompt: The Prague Spring reform movement took place in which year?
questions.hint: Warsaw Pact forces invaded Czechoslovakia that August.
questions.explanation: The Prague Spring occurred in Czechoslovakia in 1968.

questions.prompt: The Carnation Revolution of 1974 ended dictatorship in which country?
questions.hint: It also accelerated decolonization in Africa.
questions.explanation: Portugal's Carnation Revolution peacefully overthrew the Estado Novo regime.

questions.prompt: The Zimmermann Telegram proposed a German alliance with which country against the United States?
questions.hint: Germany offered support for recovering lost territory.
questions.explanation: The 1917 telegram proposed that Mexico join Germany if the United States entered World War I.

questions.prompt: What is the capital of France?
questions.hint: The Seine runs through it.
questions.explanation: Paris is the capital and largest city of France.

questions.prompt: Which is the world's largest ocean?
questions.hint: It lies between Asia and the Americas.
questions.explanation: The Pacific is the largest and deepest ocean.

questions.prompt: The Nile River empties into which sea?
questions.hint: Its delta is in northern Egypt.
questions.explanation: The Nile forms a broad delta before entering the Mediterranean.

questions.prompt: Mount Kilimanjaro is located in which country?
questions.hint: It rises near the Kenyan border.
questions.explanation: Kilimanjaro is in northeastern Tanzania.

questions.prompt: Which country is commonly described as being shaped like a boot?
questions.hint: It extends into the Mediterranean.
questions.explanation: The Italian Peninsula is famously boot-shaped.

questions.prompt: Which river flows through Vienna?
questions.hint: It continues toward Budapest and Belgrade.
questions.explanation: Vienna lies on the Danube River.

questions.prompt: The Strait of Gibraltar separates Europe from which continent?
questions.hint: Morocco lies across from Spain.
questions.explanation: The strait separates southern Spain from northern Morocco.

questions.prompt: What is the world's largest island, excluding continents?
questions.hint: It is an autonomous territory within the Kingdom of Denmark.
questions.explanation: Greenland is the world's largest island.

questions.prompt: The Atacama Desert lies primarily in which country?
questions.hint: It stretches along the Pacific coast west of the Andes.
questions.explanation: Most of the Atacama Desert is in northern Chile.

questions.prompt: Which lake is the world's deepest by maximum depth?
questions.hint: It is located in Siberia.
questions.explanation: Lake Baikal in Russia is the deepest lake on Earth.

questions.prompt: Which country is completely surrounded by South Africa?
questions.hint: Its entire border is with one country.
questions.explanation: Lesotho is an enclave within South Africa.

questions.prompt: The Wakhan Corridor is a narrow eastern extension of which country?
questions.hint: It reaches toward China between Tajikistan and Pakistan.
questions.explanation: The Wakhan Corridor is part of northeastern Afghanistan.

questions.prompt: Nakhchivan is an exclave of which country?
questions.hint: It is separated from the country's main territory by Armenia.
questions.explanation: The Nakhchivan Autonomous Republic is an exclave of Azerbaijan.

questions.prompt: The Okavango Delta is primarily located in which country?
questions.hint: The river spreads into the Kalahari instead of reaching the sea.
questions.explanation: The Okavango forms a vast inland delta in Botswana.

questions.prompt: Which country borders both the Caspian Sea and the Persian Gulf?
questions.hint: It stretches from the South Caucasus to the Gulf.
questions.explanation: Iran has coastlines on the Caspian Sea in the north and the Persian Gulf in the south.

questions.prompt: Which planet is known as the Red Planet?
questions.hint: Iron minerals give its surface a reddish color.
questions.explanation: Mars is commonly called the Red Planet because of iron oxides in its soil.

questions.prompt: What is Earth's natural satellite?
questions.hint: It drives most ocean tides.
questions.explanation: The Moon is Earth's only natural satellite.

questions.prompt: Which is the largest planet in the Solar System?
questions.hint: It has the Great Red Spot.
questions.explanation: Jupiter is the largest planet in the Solar System.

questions.prompt: What is the closest star to Earth?
questions.hint: Earth orbits it.
questions.explanation: The Sun is a star and is by far the closest one to Earth.

questions.prompt: The Milky Way is best classified as what type of galaxy?
questions.hint: A central bar runs through its spiral structure.
questions.explanation: The Milky Way is a barred spiral galaxy.

questions.prompt: What is Saturn's largest moon?
questions.hint: It has a thick nitrogen-rich atmosphere.
questions.explanation: Titan is Saturn's largest moon.

questions.prompt: A light-year is a unit of what?
questions.hint: It is how far light travels in one year.
questions.explanation: A light-year measures distance, not time.

questions.prompt: The main asteroid belt lies between the orbits of which two planets?
questions.hint: Ceres is located there.
questions.explanation: The main asteroid belt occupies the region between Mars and Jupiter.

questions.prompt: In black-hole physics, what is the event horizon?

choices.text: The boundary beyond which escape is impossible
The hottest layer of a star

questions.hint: Even light cannot return after crossing it.
questions.explanation: The event horizon is the boundary beyond which no signal can escape a black hole.

questions.prompt: What was the first exoplanet discovered orbiting a Sun-like star?
questions.hint: It was announced in 1995.
questions.explanation: 51 Pegasi b was the first confirmed exoplanet found around a main-sequence star similar to the Sun.

questions.prompt: The Chandrasekhar limit concerns the maximum stable mass of what object?
questions.hint: Above it, electron degeneracy pressure cannot support the star.
questions.explanation: The Chandrasekhar limit is the approximate maximum mass of a stable white dwarf.

questions.prompt: The Hubble sequence is a classification system for what?
questions.hint: It includes elliptical, spiral, and irregular forms.
questions.explanation: The Hubble sequence classifies galaxies by their visible morphology.

questions.prompt: The James Webb Space Telescope operates near which Sun-Earth Lagrange point?
questions.hint: It lies beyond Earth on the side away from the Sun.
questions.explanation: JWST orbits near the Sun-Earth L2 point.

questions.prompt: Which sequence correctly orders stellar spectral classes from hottest to coolest?

choices.text: A, B, C, D, E, F, G
O, B, A, F, G, K, M
O, A, B, G, F, K, M
M, K, G, F, A, B, O

questions.hint: The mnemonic begins 'Oh, Be A Fine...'.
questions.explanation: The standard temperature sequence is OBAFGKM.

questions.prompt: The Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff limit concerns the maximum mass of which object?
questions.hint: Beyond it, collapse toward a black hole is expected.
questions.explanation: The TOV limit is the upper mass limit for a stable neutron star under a given equation of state.

questions.prompt: What is the chemical formula for water?
questions.hint: It contains two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.
questions.explanation: Water has the chemical formula H₂O.

questions.prompt: Which force pulls objects toward Earth?
questions.hint: It gives objects weight.
questions.explanation: Gravity attracts masses toward one another.

questions.prompt: Which organelle is often called the powerhouse of the cell?
questions.hint: It produces much of a cell's ATP.
questions.explanation: Mitochondria generate much of the usable energy in eukaryotic cells.

questions.prompt: A solution with a pH of 7 is generally described as what?
questions.hint: Pure water is the usual reference.
questions.explanation: At room temperature, pH 7 is neutral.

questions.prompt: What shape is associated with the structure of DNA?
questions.hint: Watson and Crick's model has two intertwined strands.
questions.explanation: DNA's two strands form a double helix.

questions.prompt: Which element has the chemical symbol Na?
questions.hint: The symbol comes from the Latin natrium.
questions.explanation: Na is the chemical symbol for sodium.

questions.prompt: Newton's second law is commonly written as which equation?
questions.hint: Force equals mass times acceleration.
questions.explanation: Newton's second law relates net force, mass, and acceleration as F = ma.

questions.prompt: Avogadro's constant gives the number of constituent particles in what amount of substance?
questions.hint: Its value is about 6.022 × 10²³.
questions.explanation: Avogadro's constant is the number of specified entities in one mole.

questions.prompt: Which enzyme breaks down lactose?
questions.hint: Its deficiency causes lactose intolerance.
questions.explanation: Lactase hydrolyzes lactose into simpler sugars.

questions.prompt: The Pauli exclusion principle applies most directly to which class of particles?
questions.hint: No two identical ones can occupy the same quantum state.
questions.explanation: The Pauli exclusion principle governs identical fermions such as electrons.

questions.prompt: In eukaryotic cells, the Krebs cycle occurs primarily in which organelle?
questions.hint: It is part of aerobic cellular respiration.
questions.explanation: The Krebs cycle occurs mainly in the mitochondrial matrix.

questions.prompt: Compounds with the same molecular formula but different structures are called what?
questions.hint: Their atoms are connected or arranged differently.
questions.explanation: Isomers share a molecular formula but differ in structure.

questions.prompt: The Hall effect produces a voltage in what direction relative to an electric current and magnetic field?
questions.hint: Charge carriers are deflected sideways.
questions.explanation: The Hall voltage develops across a conductor transverse to the current.

questions.prompt: Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium assumes, among other conditions, no selection, no migration, and what kind of mating?
questions.hint: Allele frequencies remain stable under idealized conditions.
questions.explanation: Random mating is one of the classic Hardy-Weinberg assumptions.

questions.prompt: Noether's theorem links continuous symmetries to what?
questions.hint: Time-translation symmetry, for example, is tied to energy.
questions.explanation: Noether's theorem shows that continuous symmetries imply corresponding conserved quantities.

questions.prompt: Which group of animals feeds its young with milk?
questions.hint: The defining glands give the group its name.
questions.explanation: Mammals produce milk for their young.

questions.prompt: Which green pigment is central to photosynthesis?
questions.hint: It absorbs light in plant leaves.
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll captures light energy for photosynthesis.

questions.prompt: What is the largest animal known to have lived?
questions.hint: It is a marine mammal.
questions.explanation: The blue whale is the largest known animal by mass.

questions.prompt: Molten rock beneath Earth's surface is called what?
questions.hint: It is called something else after it erupts.
questions.explanation: Molten rock underground is magma; at the surface it is lava.

questions.prompt: A caterpillar becoming a butterfly is an example of what process?
questions.hint: The animal changes body form between life stages.
questions.explanation: Butterflies undergo complete metamorphosis.

questions.prompt: Many reef-building corals live in symbiosis with what organisms?
questions.hint: They are commonly called zooxanthellae.
questions.explanation: Corals often host photosynthetic dinoflagellates that provide energy.

questions.prompt: Tectonic plates move over which softer layer of the upper mantle?
questions.hint: It lies beneath the rigid lithosphere.
questions.explanation: The lithospheric plates move over the ductile asthenosphere.

questions.prompt: El Niño involves unusual warming in which region?

choices.text: The central and eastern tropical Pacific

questions.hint: It alters global weather patterns.
questions.explanation: El Niño is characterized by warm surface waters in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific.

questions.prompt: A species with a disproportionately large ecological effect relative to its abundance is called what?
questions.hint: Removing it can transform an ecosystem.
questions.explanation: Keystone species exert unusually strong effects on ecosystem structure.

questions.prompt: The Mohorovičić discontinuity separates Earth's crust from what?
questions.hint: Seismic waves change speed across it.
questions.explanation: The Moho is the boundary between the crust and mantle.

questions.prompt: Thermohaline circulation is driven mainly by differences in temperature and what else?
questions.hint: Both factors affect seawater density.
questions.explanation: Temperature and salinity differences drive density-based ocean circulation.

questions.prompt: A mycorrhiza is a symbiotic association between a fungus and what?
questions.hint: The fungus helps with nutrient uptake.
questions.explanation: Mycorrhizae are partnerships between fungi and plant roots.

questions.prompt: A rain shadow usually forms on which side of a mountain range?
questions.hint: Air has already lost much of its moisture after rising.
questions.explanation: Descending air on the leeward side becomes warmer and drier.

questions.prompt: The Cambrian explosion refers to a rapid diversification of what?
questions.hint: It occurred more than 500 million years ago.
questions.explanation: The Cambrian explosion saw the rapid appearance of many major animal groups in the fossil record.

questions.prompt: The Wilson cycle describes the repeated opening and closing of what?
questions.hint: It is tied to continental rifting and collision.
questions.explanation: The Wilson cycle explains how ocean basins form, widen, shrink, and close through plate tectonics.

questions.prompt: What does CPU stand for?
questions.hint: It executes instructions in a computer.
questions.explanation: CPU stands for Central Processing Unit.

questions.prompt: In QR code, what does QR stand for?
questions.hint: The name emphasizes rapid scanning.
questions.explanation: QR stands for Quick Response.

questions.prompt: GPS determines position primarily by receiving signals from what?
questions.hint: The transmitters orbit Earth.
questions.explanation: GPS receivers calculate position using signals from navigation satellites.

questions.prompt: Binary notation uses which two digits?
questions.hint: Each position represents a power of two.
questions.explanation: Binary numbers use only 0 and 1.

questions.prompt: Who invented the World Wide Web?
questions.hint: He proposed it while working at CERN.
questions.explanation: Tim Berners-Lee created the foundational technologies of the World Wide Web.

questions.prompt: The transistor was first demonstrated at which research institution?
questions.hint: Bardeen, Brattain, and Shockley worked there.
questions.explanation: The first working transistor was demonstrated at Bell Laboratories in 1947.

questions.prompt: RAID is commonly used to combine drives for performance, redundancy, or both. What does the R stand for?
questions.hint: The acronym describes an array designed to tolerate drive failures.
questions.explanation: RAID stands for Redundant Array of Independent Disks.

normalizationRepairs.normalizedValue: The acronym describes an array designed to tolerate drive failures.

questions.prompt: Public-key cryptography uses what kind of key arrangement?

choices.text: A new password for every bit
A mathematically related public and private key pair

questions.hint: One key can be published while the other stays secret.
questions.explanation: Public-key systems use paired public and private keys.

questions.prompt: Moore's law originally described the growth of what?

choices.text: The number of components on integrated circuits

questions.hint: It is often paraphrased as transistor counts doubling periodically.
questions.explanation: Moore's law observed rapid growth in component density on integrated circuits.

questions.prompt: Which internet protocol is responsible for reliable, ordered delivery of a byte stream?
questions.hint: It uses acknowledgments and retransmission.
questions.explanation: TCP provides reliable, ordered transport between endpoints.

questions.prompt: Byzantine fault tolerance concerns systems that remain reliable even when some components do what?
questions.hint: The name comes from the Byzantine Generals Problem.
questions.explanation: Byzantine fault-tolerant systems cope with arbitrary or deceptive failures.

questions.prompt: In a classic von Neumann architecture, instructions and data share what?
questions.hint: This shared path can create a bottleneck.
questions.explanation: Von Neumann machines store instructions and data in a common memory.

questions.prompt: Kerckhoffs's principle says a cryptosystem should remain secure even if what is public?
questions.hint: Security should not depend on hiding the algorithm.
questions.explanation: Kerckhoffs's principle places security in the secrecy of the key, not the design.

questions.prompt: The CAP theorem says a distributed system facing a network partition cannot simultaneously guarantee consistency and what?
questions.hint: The third letter refers to partition tolerance.
questions.explanation: Under a partition, a distributed system must trade between consistency and availability.

questions.prompt: Lamport clocks are used to represent what in distributed systems?
questions.hint: They help describe causality without synchronized wall clocks.
questions.explanation: Lamport logical clocks assign timestamps that preserve happened-before ordering.

questions.prompt: What is 7 + 8?
questions.hint: Add 7 to 8.

questions.prompt: What is 12 × 3?
questions.hint: Three groups of twelve.
questions.explanation: 12 multiplied by 3 equals 36.

questions.prompt: What is 100 − 37?
questions.hint: Subtract 30, then 7.

questions.prompt: What is three-quarters of 20?
questions.hint: Divide 20 by 4, then multiply by 3.
questions.explanation: One quarter of 20 is 5, so three quarters is 15.

questions.prompt: What is 15% of 80?
questions.hint: Ten percent is 8 and five percent is 4.

questions.prompt: What is the average of 8, 12, and 16?
questions.hint: Add the three values and divide by 3.
questions.explanation: The sum is 36, and 36 ÷ 3 = 12.

questions.prompt: What is 2⁵ + 3?
questions.hint: First evaluate the power.

questions.prompt: A total of 40 is divided in the ratio 3:5. What is the smaller share?
questions.hint: There are 8 equal parts in all.
questions.explanation: Each part is 5, so the smaller share is 3 × 5 = 15.

questions.prompt: What is 1/3 + 1/4?
questions.hint: Use a common denominator of 12.
questions.explanation: 1/3 is 4/12 and 1/4 is 3/12, totaling 7/12.

questions.prompt: If 5 equally productive workers finish a job in 12 days, how many days would 10 workers need?
questions.hint: Doubling the workforce halves the time under the stated assumption.
questions.explanation: The work requires 60 worker-days, so 10 workers need 6 days.

questions.prompt: What is the sum of the integers from 1 through 20?
questions.hint: Pair the first and last numbers.
questions.explanation: The sum is 20 × 21 ÷ 2 = 210.

questions.prompt: If a fair coin is tossed three times, what is the probability of exactly two heads?
questions.hint: There are three placements for the single tail.
questions.explanation: Three of the eight equally likely outcomes contain exactly two heads.

questions.prompt: What is 99²?
What is the least positive integer divisible by 6, 8, and 15?
questions.hint: Find the least common multiple.

questions.prompt: If x + 1/x = 3, what is x² + 1/x²?
questions.hint: Square the given expression and subtract 2.
questions.explanation: (x + 1/x)² = x² + 2 + 1/x² = 9, so the requested value is 7.

questions.prompt: What does 'benevolent' mean?
questions.hint: Think of goodwill toward others.
questions.explanation: Benevolent means well-meaning, kind, or charitable.

questions.prompt: What does 'concise' mean?
questions.hint: It describes economical wording.
questions.explanation: Concise language expresses much in few words.

questions.prompt: If a statement is 'ambiguous,' what is true of it?

choices.text: It can be understood in more than one way

questions.hint: Its meaning is not uniquely clear.
questions.explanation: Ambiguous language permits multiple interpretations.

questions.prompt: What does it mean to 'mitigate' a problem?
questions.hint: The word is common in discussions of risk.
questions.explanation: To mitigate something is to reduce its seriousness or harmfulness.

questions.prompt: What does 'ubiquitous' mean?
questions.hint: Smartphones are often described this way.
questions.explanation: Ubiquitous means widespread or seemingly everywhere.

questions.prompt: A 'laconic' reply is typically what?
questions.hint: The adjective is associated with the Spartans of Laconia.
questions.explanation: Laconic speech uses very few words.

questions.prompt: To 'equivocate' is to do what?
questions.hint: It can be a way to avoid commitment.
questions.explanation: To equivocate is to speak ambiguously or evasively.

questions.prompt: What does 'inchoate' mean?
questions.hint: It often describes an early-stage idea.
questions.explanation: Inchoate means only partly formed, disorganized, or undeveloped.

questions.prompt: What does 'pellucid' mean when applied to prose?
questions.hint: Its literal history relates to light passing through.
questions.explanation: Pellucid means transparently clear in style or meaning.

questions.prompt: A 'recalcitrant' person is best described as what?
questions.hint: The word often describes defiance of authority.
questions.explanation: Recalcitrant means obstinately uncooperative or resistant.

questions.prompt: What does 'apodictic' mean?
questions.hint: It describes certainty rather than probability.
